Darlowo Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Rusko, Poland

Not demolished. This cemetery, serving Darłowo's small Jewish community — never more than about 3 percent of the town's population — was established in the first half of the 19th century near the village of Rusko. During Kristallnacht in 1938, the matzevot were overturned and a memorial plaque honoring local Jewish soldiers who died serving in the German army during WWI was destroyed. Sold to a private buyer in 1974 for development despite its 1987 entry into the national monuments register, the resulting land dispute eventually reached the European Court of Human Rights in Strasbourg in 2011. Clearance work in 1992–93 uncovered about 20 damaged tombstones dating from 1860 to 1890, whose names matched historical community membership records; by 1998, only a single legible tombstone remained, that of Sarah Jacobi.
